title: Create and organize a GameObject
summary: Create an empty or primitive GameObject, name it clearly, and place it in the Hierarchy.
example_questions: How do I create an object?
Where do I add a new GameObject?
How can I organize objects in the Hierarchy?
Create an empty parent object
prerequisites: A Unity scene is open
steps: In the Hierarchy, right-click an empty area.
Choose Create Empty, or choose a primitive from the 3D Object or 2D Object submenu.
Rename the new object to describe its role.
Use the Transform component to set its position, rotation, and scale.
verification: Confirm the object appears in both the Hierarchy and Scene view.
Select it and verify that its Transform appears in the Inspector.
common_mistakes: Editing an object while Play Mode is active and losing the change afterward.
Leaving many objects with generic names such as GameObject or Cube.

title: Add a component to a GameObject
summary: Use the Inspector to add behaviour such as physics, rendering, audio, or scripts to the selected object.
example_questions: How do I add a component?
Where is Add Component?
How do I attach behaviour to an object?
Put a script on my player
prerequisites: A GameObject exists in the active scene
steps: Select the target GameObject in the Hierarchy.
At the bottom of its Inspector, click Add Component.
Search for the component by name and select it.
Configure the new component's exposed fields.
verification: Confirm the component is listed on the selected object's Inspector.
common_mistakes: Adding the component to the wrong selected object.
Searching for a script that still has compilation errors.

title: Create and assign a material
summary: Create a Material asset, select a compatible shader, and assign it to a renderer.
example_questions: How do I change an object's color?
How do I put a material on a cube?
Assign a texture to an object
Why is my object pink?
prerequisites: A rendered 3D object exists
The active render pipeline is known
steps: In the Project window, right-click inside an Assets folder and choose Create > Material.
Name the material and choose a shader compatible with the project's render pipeline.
Set its base color and optional texture.
Drag the material onto the object in the Scene view or into its renderer's Materials list.
verification: Confirm the object's appearance changes in the Scene and Game views.
common_mistakes: Using a Built-in shader in URP or HDRP, which can produce a pink material.
Changing a shared material when an object-specific copy was intended.

title: Make a 3D object respond to physics
summary: Add a Rigidbody and an appropriate 3D Collider so an object can fall and collide.
example_questions: How do I make an object fall?
How do I enable physics?
Make my cube react to gravity
My object passes through the floor
prerequisites: The moving object and floor exist in a 3D scene
steps: Select the moving object and add a Rigidbody component.
Add a suitable 3D Collider if the object does not already have one.
Ensure the floor has a 3D Collider.
Enter Play Mode and observe the object.
verification: The object falls due to gravity and stops on the floor.
common_mistakes: Mixing Rigidbody2D or Collider2D with 3D physics components.
Enabling Is Kinematic while expecting gravity to move the object.
Moving a Rigidbody by changing Transform every frame.

title: Make a 2D object respond to physics
summary: Add Rigidbody2D and Collider2D components to participate in Unity's separate 2D physics system.
example_questions: How do I add 2D physics?
Make my sprite fall
My 2D player passes through platforms
Rigidbody2D setup
prerequisites: A Sprite or other 2D GameObject exists
steps: Select the moving 2D object and add Rigidbody2D.
Add an appropriate Collider2D to the moving object.
Ensure platforms have Collider2D components.
Enter Play Mode to test the interaction.
verification: The object responds to 2D gravity and collides with the platform.
common_mistakes: Mixing 2D and 3D physics components.
Using a trigger collider when a solid collision was intended.

title: Respond to a collision in a script
summary: Use the correct 2D or 3D collision callback on a MonoBehaviour attached to a participating object.
example_questions: How do I detect a collision?
Run code when objects touch
How does OnTriggerEnter work?
My collision function is not called
prerequisites: The relevant physics components are already configured
steps: Decide whether the interaction should be a physical collision or a trigger.
Attach a MonoBehaviour script to one participating object.
For 3D, implement OnCollisionEnter or OnTriggerEnter; for 2D, use the callback ending in 2D.
Log the other object's name first to verify the callback before adding gameplay logic.
verification: The Console prints once when the objects first interact.
common_mistakes: Using a 3D callback with 2D components.
Spelling or capitalizing Unity message methods incorrectly.
Having no Rigidbody on either participating object.

title: Create basic player movement
summary: Read player input, calculate a direction, and move through the appropriate physics component.
example_questions: How do I move my player?
Control a character with WASD
Basic movement script
Make the character respond to keyboard input
prerequisites: A player GameObject exists
The project input system has been chosen
steps: Choose whether the project uses the Input System package or the legacy Input Manager.
Read a two-axis movement value in a player-control script.
Normalize or clamp the direction so diagonal movement is not faster.
Apply movement through Rigidbody, Rigidbody2D, or CharacterController rather than mixing several movement systems.
verification: The player moves in every intended direction at a consistent speed.
common_mistakes: Multiplying physics movement by frame time in the wrong place.
Changing Transform directly on a dynamic Rigidbody.
Using code for a different input backend than the project setting.

title: Make a camera follow the player
summary: Configure a simple scripted follow camera or a Cinemachine camera with a player target.
example_questions: How do I make the camera follow the player?
My character walks away from the camera
Set up a third-person camera
How do I use Cinemachine follow?
prerequisites: A player object and Main Camera exist
steps: Decide between a simple fixed-offset camera and Cinemachine.
For Cinemachine, install or enable the package and create an appropriate Cinemachine camera.
Assign the player Transform to the camera's Tracking Target or Follow field.
Adjust position, damping, and framing while testing in Play Mode.
verification: Move the player and confirm that the camera maintains the intended framing.
common_mistakes: Assigning the visual child instead of the stable player root.
Having multiple enabled AudioListeners or competing active cameras.

title: Create and reuse a prefab
summary: Turn a configured scene object into a reusable Prefab asset and understand instances and overrides.
example_questions: How do I create a prefab?
Reuse the same enemy many times
What is a prefab instance?
Save a GameObject as an asset
prerequisites: A configured GameObject exists in the scene
steps: Create a Prefabs folder in Assets if one does not exist.
Drag the configured GameObject from the Hierarchy into that folder.
Create additional instances by dragging the Prefab asset into the scene.
Use the Overrides menu deliberately when applying or reverting instance changes.
verification: Edit the Prefab asset and confirm that its non-overridden instances update.
common_mistakes: Applying an unwanted scene-specific value to every instance.
Unpacking a prefab without needing to break its connection.

title: Play an animation with an Animator Controller
summary: Connect animation clips through an Animator Controller and use parameters to change states.
example_questions: How do I play an animation?
Set up an Animator Controller
Switch from idle to walk
My animation clip does not play
prerequisites: At least one compatible animation clip exists
steps: Create an Animator Controller asset.
Assign it to the target object's Animator component.
Open the Animator window and drag animation clips into it as states.
Create parameters and transitions for state changes, then update those parameters from gameplay code.
verification: Enter Play Mode and watch the active state highlight in the Animator window.
common_mistakes: Leaving the Animator without a controller.
Creating a transition whose conditions can never become true.
Using clips configured for an incompatible avatar type.

title: Create a UI button that performs an action
summary: Add a Canvas and Button, then connect its On Click event to a public component method.
example_questions: How do I make a button?
Run a function when UI is clicked
Create a start button
My Unity button does nothing
prerequisites: A scene is open
steps: Create a Button through GameObject > UI; Unity also creates a Canvas and EventSystem when needed.
Select the Button and find its On Click event in the Inspector.
Add a listener, drag in the GameObject containing the target script, and select a compatible public method.
Enter Play Mode and click the button.
verification: The configured method runs exactly once when the button is clicked.
common_mistakes: Dragging the script asset instead of the scene GameObject containing the component.
Testing clicks outside Play Mode.
Missing or disabled EventSystem.

title: Change from one scene to another
summary: Add scenes to the build configuration and load them through SceneManager.
example_questions: How do I load another scene?
Change levels when a button is clicked
Go from menu to game
SceneManager setup
prerequisites: The source and destination scenes have been saved
steps: Add the destination scene to the project's build scene list or build profile.
Import UnityEngine.SceneManagement in the controlling script.
Call SceneManager.LoadScene with the intended scene name or build index.
Trigger that method from gameplay or a UI event.
verification: Enter Play Mode, trigger the transition, and confirm the destination scene loads.
common_mistakes: Misspelling a scene name.
Forgetting to include the scene in the build configuration.
Expecting ordinary scene objects to persist without DontDestroyOnLoad.

title: Play sound from a GameObject
summary: Use an AudioSource with an AudioClip and make sure the scene has exactly one active AudioListener.
example_questions: How do I play a sound?
Add background music
Play an effect when jumping
Why is there no audio?
prerequisites: An imported AudioClip exists
steps: Select the sound-producing GameObject and add an AudioSource.
Assign the AudioClip and configure volume, looping, and spatial blend.
Use Play On Awake for automatic playback or call Play/PlayOneShot from a script.
Confirm that an enabled AudioListener exists, normally on the Main Camera.
verification: Enter Play Mode and hear the clip under the intended condition.
common_mistakes: Having zero or multiple active AudioListeners.
Using full 3D spatial blend while the listener is too far away.
Muting the Game view audio toggle.

title: Set up basic lighting in a 3D scene
summary: Use directional, point, or spot lights and inspect exposure, shadows, and environment settings.
example_questions: Why is my scene dark?
How do I add lights?
Set up sunlight
My shadows look wrong
prerequisites: A rendered 3D scene exists
steps: Add or select a Directional Light for broad outdoor illumination.
Rotate it to choose the direction of light and shadows.
Adjust intensity and shadow settings for the current render pipeline.
Inspect the Environment Lighting and exposure settings if the entire scene remains too dark or bright.
verification: Objects are readable in both Scene and Game views and shadows point consistently.
common_mistakes: Changing Scene-view lighting while judging a different Game camera result.
Using extreme intensity to compensate for incorrect exposure.

title: Make an agent navigate with a NavMesh
summary: Prepare walkable geometry, build navigation data, and assign a destination to a NavMeshAgent.
example_questions: How do I make an enemy walk to the player?
Set up NavMesh
My NavMeshAgent does not move
Add pathfinding
prerequisites: Walkable level geometry exists
AI Navigation is available
steps: Install or enable the AI Navigation package if required by the Unity version.
Add a NavMeshSurface to an appropriate level object and configure what it collects.
Build the NavMesh and verify the walkable visualization.
Add NavMeshAgent to the moving character and set a reachable destination from a script.
verification: The agent follows the baked walkable area to the destination.
common_mistakes: Placing the agent away from the built NavMesh.
Using a destination outside all reachable areas.
Building navigation data before the level geometry is ready.

title: Create and attach a C# MonoBehaviour script
summary: Create a C# script, keep the class and filename aligned, and attach it to a GameObject.
example_questions: How do I create a script?
Attach C# code to an object
What are Start and Update?
My script cannot be added
prerequisites: Unity's configured code editor is available
steps: In the Project window, right-click an Assets folder and create a MonoBehaviour/C# script.
Give it a valid descriptive class name and open it in the code editor.
Use Start for initialization and Update only for work that must be checked each rendered frame.
Save the file, wait for Unity to compile, and attach it to the intended GameObject.
verification: The script appears as a component without a Missing or compilation warning.
common_mistakes: Renaming the class without matching the filename.
Trying to attach a script while any project compilation error exists.
Putting expensive work in Update unnecessarily.

title: Create a playable build
summary: Select a platform, include the correct scenes, configure player settings, and build outside the Assets folder.
example_questions: How do I export my game?
Make a Windows build
Create an executable
Which scenes are included in the build?
prerequisites: At least one saved scene is ready to run
steps: Open Build Profiles or Build Settings, depending on the Unity version.
Choose the target platform and switch to it if necessary.
Add and order every required scene, placing the startup scene first.
Review Player Settings, then build into a dedicated folder outside Assets.
verification: Launch the produced build and test scene transitions, input, audio, and quitting.
common_mistakes: Building inside the Assets folder.
Leaving the startup scene out of the build configuration.
Assuming behaviour in the Editor guarantees identical build behaviour.
